title: Link Attributes & Best Practices 🧭
description: Master `href`, `target`, `rel`, and how to write accessible, user-friendly links.

slides.title: The `target` Attribute 🎯
slides.content: # Where Should the Link Open? - `_self` (default) – opens in the same tab/window. - `_blank` – opens in a new tab or window. - `_parent` and `_top` – used with frames (rare nowadays). ```html Open in New Tab ``` Use `_blank` sparingly – it can disorient users. Reserve it for external links when you don't want to disrupt the current flow.

slides.title: The `rel` Attribute 🔐
slides.content: # Relationship Between Current and Linked Document - `noopener` – prevents the new page from accessing `window.opener` (security best practice for `target="_blank"`). - `noreferrer` – hides the referrer information. - `nofollow` – tells search engines not to pass ranking credit (for untrusted links). Example: ```html Safe External Link ``` Always pair `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener"`.

quizData.question: Why is `rel="noopener"` recommended for links with `target="_blank"`?

options.text: To make the link open faster
To prevent the new page from potentially manipulating the original page

quizData.explanation: Without `noopener`, the new tab can access the original window via `window.opener`, posing a security risk.

slides.title: Anchor to a Page Section 🔖
slides.content:
# Linking to an ID You can link to a specific part of a page using a **fragment identifier**: ```html

Frequently Asked Questions

... Jump to FAQ ``` This scrolls the page to the element with `id="faq"`. Use it for table of contents or "back to top" links.

slides.title: Smooth Scrolling Example
slides.content: Combine with CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth;` for a polished effect:
slides.codeSnippet:
Services Contact

Our Services

...

Get in Touch

...

quizData.question: To link to an element with `id="pricing"`, the href should be ______.
quizData.explanation: The fragment identifier starts with a hash (#) followed by the exact id.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Underline That Link

By default, browsers underline links. It's a strong visual cue. If you remove the underline with CSS, ensure another visual distinction (like colour contrast) remains so users know it's clickable.
